resolution: PASS (claude, 21:3xZ) as a NON-KILL row. All six RECEIPT pins match and the capacity-source pin equals the sha of q7_h7_universal_singleton_capacity.json in the shared tree. verify_witnesses.py re-run from a scratch copy: PASS 26/2. My own independent check of pilot-1.json (no search code, own adjacency reconstruction): 26 PARTIAL_WITNESS rows each give a simple 49-vertex graph with high degrees 8, empty degrees 7, highs independent, every singleton adjacent to exactly its colour and every pair vertex to exactly its pair, all C(49,2) common-neighbour counts ≤ 1, the empty-induced graph equal to the class's edge list, each empty vertex of E-degree d having exactly d pair neighbours and 7−2d singleton neighbours whose supports partition the seven colours, every singleton ≤ 2 empty neighbours and every pair vertex ≤ 1; the two UNKNOWN_AT_CAP rows are masks 6808 and 39441 (a=6), which target-join.json maps to cube_F6_t17 and cube_F6_t14 (I read the artifact, not the chat). Necessity of the searched constraints re-derived from the H7/T0 ledger: an empty vertex has 7 low neighbours whose supports partition 7 colours ⇒ (pairs, singles, empties) = (d, 7−2d, d); a pair vertex (degree 5) satisfies 2k+s=7, k+s+m=5 ⇒ m=k−2 ≤ 1 empty neighbour; a singleton (degree 6) ⇒ m=k−1 ≤ 2; two singletons sharing two empties, or one singleton's two empties already sharing an empty neighbour, would close a C4 — all necessary. Normalizations audited: the first vertex's pair matching fixed by a global colour permutation is valid because all seven colours are symmetric in T0 before any assignment, and the twin-singleton first-touch rule is valid because twins are interchangeable until used. Scope as stated: witnesses of the incidence layer only (S/P residual degrees and S–S/S–P/P–P edges unassigned), so this cannot exclude and does not; the two capped classes are unknown, not survivors. Master table gets: "H7/T0 labelled incidence: 26/28 classes admit a C4-free partial witness, 2 unknown at cap — no kill".
